title: Turning fractions into decimals
objectives: Write a fraction as a decimal by rewriting it over 10, 100 or 1000
Divide to convert any fraction, and recognise a recurring decimal
Round a recurring decimal to two decimal places

screens.title: Turning fractions into decimals
screens.prose: A fraction and a decimal can name the same amount. We will turn fractions into decimals, and meet decimals that never stop.
This square is cut into 100 equal cells. One quarter of the square is shaded.
screens.question: How many of the 100 cells are shaded?

hints.text: The shaded block is 5 cells wide.
Count one row of the shaded block, then count the rows.
5 rows of 5 cells is 25 cells.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the shaded cells row by row.

byKey.four: 4 is the bottom of $\tfrac14$. Count the shaded cells instead.
byKey.quarter-of-ten: You took a quarter of 10. The square has 100 cells, so take a quarter of 100.

explain.text: You found $\tfrac{1}{4} = \tfrac{25}{100}$, which is 25 hundredths. As a decimal that is $0.25$. We turned the fraction into hundredths, and the hundredths gave the digits.

screens.prose: The line from 0 to 1 is marked in tenths. Fifths are bigger pieces: five of them fill the line.
screens.question: Drag the point to $\tfrac{3}{5}$.

hints.text: How many tenths fit in one fifth?
Ten tenths make five fifths, so each fifth is 2 tenths. Three fifths is 6 tenths.

feedback.correct: Three fifths lands on the sixth tick: 6 tenths.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each fifth is two tenth-steps long.

byKey.three-tenths: You placed 3 tenths. A fifth is two tenths wide, so 3 fifths is 6 tenths.

explain.text: Each fifth covers 2 tenths, so $\tfrac{3}{5} = \tfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$. You turned fifths into tenths, the size the first decimal digit counts.

screens.prose: Twice now you rewrote a fraction with 10 or 100 on the bottom. Then the top gave the digits. Numbers like 10, 100 and 1000 are **powers of ten**.
screens.question: Write $\tfrac{7}{20}$ as a decimal.

hints.text: What do you multiply 20 by to make 100?
$\tfrac{7}{20} = \tfrac{7 \times 5}{20 \times 5} = \tfrac{35}{100}$. Now write 35 hundredths as a decimal.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Rewrite the fraction over 100 first.

byKey.over-ten: You treated $\tfrac{7}{20}$ as $\tfrac{7}{10}$. Twenty is twice ten, so each piece is half a tenth.
byKey.digits: You wrote the digits 7 and 2 side by side. Rewrite the fraction over 100 first.
byKey.flipped: You divided 20 by 7. The fraction means 7 divided by 20, which is less than 1.

explain.text: Multiplying top and bottom by 5 gives $\tfrac{35}{100}$, the same amount in hundredths. 35 hundredths is $0.35$. On the line it is 7 of the twentieth-steps.

screens.prose: Eight does not go into 10 or 100 exactly. It does go into 1000, because $8 \times 125 = 1000$.
screens.question: Write $\tfrac{3}{8}$ as a decimal.

hints.text: Multiply top and bottom by the same number to reach 1000.
$\tfrac{3}{8} = \tfrac{3 \times 125}{8 \times 125} = \tfrac{375}{1000}$. That is 375 thousandths.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply top and bottom by 125, then read the thousandths.

byKey.point-three: You moved the 3 behind the point. Rewrite the fraction over 1000 first.
byKey.flipped: You divided 8 by 3. The fraction means 3 divided by 8, which is less than 1.
byKey.point-three-eight: You wrote the digits 3 and 8 side by side. Rewrite the fraction over 1000 first.

explain.text: $\tfrac{3}{8} = \tfrac{375}{1000} = 0.375$: three places for thousandths. On the line it sits between $\tfrac14 = 0.25$ and $\tfrac12 = 0.5$.

screens.prose: Now try $\tfrac{1}{3}$. To use the same trick, 3 must divide a power of ten exactly.
screens.question: Which power of ten can 3 divide into exactly?

options.why: You tried 10, but 3 × 3 = 9 and 3 × 4 = 12. Dividing 10 by 3 leaves 1 over.
You tried 100, but 3 × 33 = 99. Dividing 100 by 3 leaves 1 over.
You tried 1000, but 3 × 333 = 999. Dividing 1000 by 3 leaves 1 over.

hints.text: Work out $10 \div 3$, then $100 \div 3$.
Each power of ten is one more than 9, 99 or 999. Three divides those exactly, so 1 is always left.

feedback.correct: No power of ten splits exactly into thirds.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide each power of ten by 3 and look at what is left over.

explain.text: Every power of ten is one more than 9, 99, 999 and so on, which 3 divides exactly. So there is always 1 left over. $\tfrac13$ cannot be written over 10, 100 or 1000.

screens.prose: When no power of ten works, we divide. Share 1 whole among 3, one place at a time.

steps.caption: 1 whole cannot be split into 3 whole ones. Swap it for 10 tenths. Each share gets 3 tenths, and 1 tenth is left.
Swap the leftover tenth for 10 hundredths. Each share gets 3 hundredths, and 1 hundredth is left.
Swap that for 10 thousandths. Again each share gets 3, and 1 is left.
The leftover is always 1, so the 3s never stop: $\tfrac13 = 0.333\ldots$. We write $0.\dot{3}$ and call it a **recurring** decimal.

screens.prose: The same sharing gives $\tfrac{2}{3} = 0.666\ldots$, with 6s for ever. A price screen shows only two decimal places.
screens.question: Drag the blue point to $\tfrac23$ rounded to two decimal places.

hints.text: Is $0.666\ldots$ closer to 0.66 or to 0.67?
The third digit after the point is a 6.
$0.666\ldots$ is about 0.007 above 0.66 but only about 0.003 below 0.67.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the two hundredths either side, then pick the closer.

byKey.chopped: You cut the decimal after two places. The next digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 0.67.

explain.text: $\tfrac23 = 0.666\ldots$ lies between 0.66 and 0.67, nearer 0.67. The third digit, 6, is 5 or more, so we round up. To two decimal places, $\tfrac23 \approx 0.67$.

screens.prose: A calculator set to two decimal places shows $\tfrac13$ as $0.33$.
screens.question: Is $0.33$ equal to $\tfrac13$?

options.text: Yes, they are the same number
options.why: You treated the rounded value as exact. $3 \times 0.33 = 0.99$, but $3 \times \tfrac13 = 1$.
You assumed rounding pushed it up. The 3s after 0.33 were dropped, so 0.33 is below $\tfrac13$.

hints.text: Multiply each of them by 3.
$3 \times 0.33 = 0.99$, while $3 \times \tfrac13 = 1$. Which is bigger?

byKey.equal: You treated the rounded value as exact. $3 \times 0.33 = 0.99$, not 1.

explain.text: Rounding dropped the 3s after 0.33, so $0.33$ is $\tfrac{1}{300}$ short of $\tfrac13$. Check: $3 \times 0.33 = 0.99$, not 1. A rounded decimal is close, not equal, so we write $\tfrac13 \approx 0.33$.

screens.prose: A fraction $\tfrac{a}{b}$ means $a \div b$. Powers of ten break into 2s and 5s only: $$10 = 2 \times 5, \qquad 100 = 2 \times 2 \times 5 \times 5$$ So the decimal stops when the bottom, in lowest terms, breaks into 2s and 5s only. Otherwise it recurs.
screens.question: Which fraction gives a decimal that stops?

options.why: You saw a 2 in $6 = 2 \times 3$. The 3 makes it recur: $0.1666\ldots$
You may have pictured 9 as close to 10. But $9 = 3 \times 3$, so it recurs: $0.222\ldots$
You saw the 2s in $12 = 2 \times 2 \times 3$. The 3 makes it recur: $0.41666\ldots$

hints.text: Break each bottom into small factors. Look for anything other than 2 and 5.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Break each bottom into 2s, 3s, 5s and so on.

explain.text: $40 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5$, so $\tfrac{7}{40} = \tfrac{175}{1000} = 0.175$. The others each have a 3 in the bottom, and no power of ten has a 3.

screens.prose: Going back is the same idea in reverse. Turn $0.125$ into a fraction in its lowest terms.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $0.125 = \tfrac{125}{1000}$, three places after the point means thousandths

hints.text: Which line turns the decimal into a fraction?
Write 125 thousandths first. Then shrink the top and bottom by the same number, twice.

feedback.correct: Thousandths first, then shrink top and bottom together.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start by writing the decimal as thousandths.

byKey.e2: You can only divide once there is a fraction. Start with 125 thousandths.
byKey.e3: $\tfrac18$ is the end point. It comes from $\tfrac{25}{200}$ divided by 25.

explain.text: You wrote 125 thousandths, then divided top and bottom by 5 and by 25. Dividing both by the same number keeps the amount. So $0.125 = \tfrac18$, which matches $1 \div 8 = 0.125$.

screens.prose: Your order to buy 3 shares fills in three parts, at £10.00, £10.01 and £10.01. Prices are quoted to two decimal places.
screens.question: What is the average price per share, to two decimal places?

hints.text: Add the three prices, then share the total by 3.
The total is £30.02.
$30.02 \div 3 = 10.00666\ldots$. Round that to two places.

feedback.correct: The average is £10.00666..., which rounds to £10.01.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the total by 3, then round to two places.

byKey.chopped: You cut after two places. The next digit is 6, so the pennies round up to £10.01.
byKey.unrounded: That is the exact average. Quote it to two places: the third digit is 6, so round up.

explain.text: $30.02 \div 3 = 10.00666\ldots$, a recurring decimal. The third place is 6, so it rounds up to £10.01. Quotes stop at whole pennies, so recurring averages always get rounded.

ideas: To convert a fraction, rewrite it over 10, 100 or 1000, or divide the top by the bottom.
A decimal stops when the bottom, in lowest terms, breaks into 2s and 5s only. Otherwise it recurs.
A rounded recurring decimal is close but not equal: $\tfrac13 \approx 0.33$.

formula.name: Fraction to decimal
formula.note: When no power of ten works, divide: $\tfrac13 = 1 \div 3 = 0.\dot{3}$.

summary.trap: $0.33$ is not $\tfrac13$. It is $\tfrac{1}{300}$ short, so write $\tfrac13 \approx 0.33$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply top and bottom by 4.

byKey.digits: You wrote 9 and 25 side by side. Multiply top and bottom by 4 to get hundredths.
byKey.flipped: You divided 25 by 9. The fraction means 9 divided by 25.
byKey.over-ten: You moved the 9 behind the point, as if the bottom were 10. It is 25.

quiz.prose: $\tfrac{5}{6}$ means $5 \div 6$, which is $0.8333\ldots$ with 3s for ever.
quiz.question: What is $\tfrac{5}{6}$ to two decimal places?

options.why: You rounded up, but the third digit is 3, which is below 5.
You put the 5 and the 6 after the point. $\tfrac56$ means 5 divided by 6.
You stopped at one decimal place. Two places means hundredths.

feedback.correct: The third digit is 3, so round down to 0.83.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look at the third digit after the point.

explain.text: $0.8333\ldots$ lies between 0.83 and 0.84. The third digit, 3, is below 5, so we round down: $\tfrac56 \approx 0.83$.

quiz.prose: The bottom of $\tfrac{3}{12}$ is $12 = 2 \times 2 \times 3$, which has a 3 in it.
quiz.question: Does $\tfrac{3}{12}$ give a decimal that stops?

options.text: No: the 3 in 12 makes it recur
options.why: You checked the bottom before simplifying. $\tfrac{3}{12} = \tfrac14$, and $4 = 2 \times 2$.
You worked out $1 \div 3$. Here it is $3 \div 12$, which is $0.25$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put the fraction in lowest terms first.

explain.text: Divide top and bottom by 3: $\tfrac{3}{12} = \tfrac{1}{4}$. Now the bottom is $2 \times 2$, so the decimal stops: $0.25$. Always simplify before you check the bottom.

quiz.prose: A £100 profit is split equally between 3 partners. Each payment is made to the penny.
quiz.question: How much does each partner get?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide by 3, then round to two decimal places.

byKey.up: You rounded up, but the third digit is 3, which is below 5.
byKey.one-place: You stopped at one decimal place. Pennies are hundredths, so give two.
byKey.unrounded: Payments stop at whole pennies. Round to two decimal places.

explain.text: $100 \div 3 = 33.333\ldots$, a recurring decimal. To the penny that is £33.33. Three payments of £33.33 make £99.99, so 1p is left over.
